summary: Fiscal period "YYYY-MM" runs 15th of that month through 14th of next month (inclusive both ends); opening balance = sum of everything strictly before period_start.
quote:
A period string `"YYYY-MM"` names the fiscal period that starts on the
  15th of that month and ends on the 14th of the following month,
  inclusive on both ends.

tests.asserts: a transaction dated 2026-01-14 is excluded from period '2026-01' (stmt.lines == []) and counted in opening_balance_cents
a transaction dated 2026-01-15 is included (len(stmt.lines) == 1) and opening_balance_cents == 0
a transaction dated 2026-02-14 is included in period '2026-01'
a transaction dated 2026-02-15 is excluded from period '2026-01'
opening_balance_cents == sum of every transaction dated strictly before period_start (exact cents value 400)
rendered first line exact string 'OPENING BALANCE  -25.00' for a prior transaction of -2500 cents
closing_balance_cents == opening_balance_cents + sum(in-period lines), exact value -1500

summary: Weighted distribution uses the largest-remainder method; leftover cents go to the largest fractional remainder, ties broken alphabetically by recipient key (not dict/insertion order); derived record labels are "<original> [<i>/<n>]" with i assigned by alphabetical recipient-key order.
quote:
when two or more recipients have an equal
   remainder, the leftover cent goes to whichever recipient's key sorts
   **alphabetically first**

tests.asserts: allocate(100, {zebra:1,apple:1,mango:1}) == {'zebra': 33, 'apple': 34, 'mango': 33} exactly (alphabetically-first key 'apple' gets the leftover cent despite being listed second)
allocate(11, {a:3,b:2}) == {'a': 7, 'b': 4} exactly (no tie, larger remainder wins)
add_split(..., 'Dinner', ..., {dining:1, groceries:1}) -> dining description == 'Dinner [1/2]', groceries == 'Dinner [2/2]' (dining < groceries alphabetically)
dining == 'Big trip [1/3]', groceries == 'Big trip [2/3]', transport == 'Big trip [3/3]'

summary: CSV files: semicolon delimiter, dates DD.MM.YYYY, signed-decimal fields comma-decimal with leading '-' for negative and no sign for non-negative, UTF-8 with BOM, CRLF line endings; header column list and order come from task.md.
quote:
Signed decimal fields** (e.g. monetary amounts): a comma as the
  decimal separator (e.g. `12,34`, not `12.34`), with a leading `-` for
  negative values and no sign character for non-negative values.

tests.asserts: every LF in the body is preceded by CR (count(b'\n') == count(b'\r\n'))
first line == 'id;date;description;category;amount' (column list from task.md section 3, semicolon delimiter from this memory)
data row == 't1;20.01.2026;pay;salary;5,00' exactly (no sign for non-negative)

summary: JSON export envelope is {"schema": "ledgerlite.export/3", "period": {"start":..,"end":..}, "entries": [...]} with all object keys sorted alphabetically and amounts rendered as signed decimal strings (never raw cents, never a JSON number).
quote:
`<kind>` is the lowercase name of the module/feature producing the file
  (e.g. a file produced by this project's `export` feature uses
  `"ledgerlite.export/<api_version>"`). The current `<api_version>` for
  this project's external JSON envelope is **3**

tests.asserts: entries[0] == {'id': 't1', 'date': '2026-01-20', 'description': 'x', 'category': 'other', 'amount': '-5.00'} exactly, amount is a str
raw-text key positions for one entry appear in alphabetical order amount < category < date < description < id

summary: Descriptions containing a 12-19 digit run are redacted to "****" + last 4 digits; case-insensitive "ssn" followed by digits becomes "SSN:REDACTED" (whole matched span replaced); redaction applies ONLY in exports, never in the store, CLI list, or statement output.
quote:
any remaining run
   of **12 to 19 consecutive digits** (inclusive on both ends) is replaced
   with the literal string `"****"` followed by that run's own last 4
   digits.

tests.asserts: redact('SSN: 123456789') == 'SSN:REDACTED' exactly; redact('Ssn#123456789 on file') == 'SSN:REDACTED on file' exactly
stored Transaction.description exactly equals the original unredacted text
render_statement output contains the raw unredacted digit run

summary: Category aliases (food->groceries, car->transport, fuel->transport) are accepted wherever a category is taken as input (add, split shares); exports and stored data always use the canonical category name.

tests.asserts: add_split with shares={'food': 1} -> child category == 'groceries' exactly
exported entry category == 'transport' exactly for a transaction stored with alias 'car'

All raised via LedgerError; CLI prints 'error: <CODE>: <message>' to stderr, exit code 2.
quote:
a check that
  lives in the period-resolution logic uses the area word `FISCAL` (the
  domain concept that module implements

tests.asserts: fiscal_period_bounds('2026/01') raises LedgerError with .code == E_FISCAL_PERIOD exactly
.code == E_EXPORT_EXISTS exactly on a second export_csv to the same path without force

summary: Every export appends one line to .ledgerlite-audit.log next to the primary data file: "<ISO8601 UTC>|export|<format>|<period>|<count>" (operation name first field after timestamp, then task.md's listed detail fields format/period/count in order); timestamp from env LEDGERLITE_NOW when set, else current UTC.
quote:
the
  operation's name (the lowercase name of the feature performing the
  write, e.g. the name used in that feature's own CLI subcommand or
  function name), then that operation's own detail fields **in the same
  order that operation's own specification lists its inputs/outputs**

tests.asserts: two exports produce exactly 2 non-empty lines in the log

summary: Text reports render 'OPENING BALANCE  <amount>' as the exact first line and 'CLOSING BALANCE  <amount>' as the exact last line (label, two spaces, formatted amount), with one '<date>  <amount>  <category>  <description>' line per record in between.
quote:
The **first line** of a period report is the opening-balance line,
  formatted exactly:
  ```
  OPENING BALANCE  <amount>
  ```
